app.message: services.conflict-b.ports[0] publishes 8080/tcp, already published by services.conflict-a.ports[0]
app.hint: Publish each node port from one service only.

app.message: Service host-dup binds node ports, so replicas are replaced stop-first (brief downtime per replica)
app.hint: Publish through the load balancer (remove `mode: host` or `x-dockflow.publish: hostport`) to keep start-first updates.

app.message: services.host-dup.ports[1] binds container port 9100/tcp on the node a second time
app.hint: Bind the container port once in `mode: host`, or use the default ingress mode.

app.message: host-replicas binds node port 9500/tcp and runs 3 replicas, but two pods cannot bind one port on one node
app.hint: Publish through the load balancer (`x-dockflow.publish: loadbalancer`), or run one pod per node with `deploy.mode: global`.

app.message: Service host-replicas binds node ports, so replicas are replaced stop-first (brief downtime per replica)
app.hint: Publish through the load balancer (remove `mode: host` or `x-dockflow.publish: hostport`) to keep start-first updates.

app.message: services.loopback-lb.ports[0] binds 127.0.0.1, which a load balancer publishing on every node cannot honour
app.hint: Remove the address to publish on every node, use `expose` for in-cluster access only, or set `x-dockflow.publish: hostport` to bind it on the node running the pod.

app.message: services.sctp-svc.ports[0] publishes 5000/sctp through the load balancer, which forwards only TCP and UDP
app.hint: Set `x-dockflow.publish: hostport` to bind the port on the node running the pod, or use `expose` for in-cluster access only.

app.message: Service too-many publishes 11 ports through its load balancer; ServiceLB runs one container per port on every node, so at most 10 are accepted
app.hint: Publish fewer ports, or set `x-dockflow.publish: hostport`.
